summary:
Project PAF (Planetary Analog Finder) is an interactive comparative planetology web platform that helps scientists and mission planners identify locations on Earth that closely replicate the geological, topographic, and environmental conditions of future landing sites on the Moon and Mars.
Using real multi-agency remote sensing datasets (NASA LRO/MOLA/PDS, ESA Copernicus, CSA RADARSAT), our engine evaluates 1,420 sites across an 8-dimensional parameter space—including surface roughness, slope, elevation, temperature, and UV radiation—combining Cosine, Euclidean, and Manhattan similarity metrics with customizable feature weights and custom CSV/coordinate inputs. When tested on NASA’s Artemis candidate site de Gerlache Rim 2, Project PAF validated known analogs like McMurdo Dry Valleys while uncovering new, previously undocumented terrestrial analog candidates.
By replacing manual guesswork with objective, reproducible data modeling, Project PAF reduces hardware testing risks and lowers preparation costs for future human and robotic deep-space missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Planetary Analog Finder is an interactive comparative planetology web platform designed to help scientists, mission planners, and engineers identify locations on Earth that closely replicate the geological, topographic, and environmental conditions of future landing sites on the Moon and Mars.
The engine evaluates planetary and terrestrial sites across an 8-dimensional parameter space: surface roughness (RMS height), elevation, mean slope, mean temperature, mineralization, UV index, relative humidity, and atmospheric pressure. Using min-max normalization across celestial bodies, the platform computes similarity scores via three independent mathematical metrics—Cosine Similarity, Euclidean Distance, and Manhattan Distance—and displays an overall consensus score. Users can explore pre-loaded iconic landing sites (such as Apollo 11, Curiosity, Viking 2, and Artemis candidates), input custom coordinates, upload custom CSV datasets, dynamically adjust feature weights (0.0–5.0), set a Top-N threshold, and visualize results through interactive 3D globes, multi-axis radar charts, and 2D PCA feature-space projections.

Key Benefits & Scientific Validity

• Objective, Data-Driven Selection: Replaces manual guesswork with reproducible multi-metric ranking, achieving a 92.6% match accuracy (~7.4% error margin) when benchmarked against officially recognized NASA terrestrial analogs.
• Real-World Discovery for Artemis: Using our custom query feature, we evaluated de Gerlache Rim 2—a primary candidate landing region near the Lunar South Pole for NASA’s Artemis program—and generated the top 20 terrestrial analogs. Alongside established analogs like McMurdo Dry Valleys (Score: 0.8748) and Haughton Crater (0.8673), our algorithm uncovered previously undocumented analog candidates with matching cryogenic and topographic profiles, including Batagaika Crater in Yakutia (0.8700), Popigai Crater (0.8662), and Putorana Plateau (0.8636).
• Full Scientific Transparency: A dedicated Methodology tab documents every equation, worked calculation example (Gale Crater), and exact satellite data source, alongside a one-click CSV export for researchers.

Intended Impact

Testing rovers, spacesuits, drills, and habitats in deep space carries immense financial and operational risk. By matching specific mission profiles—such as high-slope rover navigation or sub-zero regolith drilling—to precise earthly counterparts, Planetary Analog Finder reduces hardware failure risks, lowers mission preparation costs, and democratizes access to complex planetary remote-sensing data for researchers, students, and space agencies worldwide.

Tools, Programming Languages & Data Sources

• Languages & Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), JSON, and custom TopoJSON geodata.
• Visualization & Analytics: Plotly.js for interactive 3D globes (Earth, Mars, Moon), normalized radar profiles, and Principal Component Analysis (PC₁ vs. PC₂) scatter plots; Python and QGIS for preprocessing Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and elevation matrices.
• Space Agency Datasets: Built using authentic open-source records from NASA (PDS, LRO LOLA/LROC/Diviner, MOLA, HiRISE, CRISM, MERRA-2, Earthdata), ESA (Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, Mars Climate Database), CSA (RADARSAT-1 / RCM), and JAXA (G-Portal).

Creativity & Innovation

Unlike static maps or single-metric dashboards, our platform combines multi-engine distance comparison with real-time parametric weighting and client-side custom CSV ingestion. Furthermore, we solved the challenge of sparse planetary data by implementing a Missing Parameter Penalization control and spatial data augmentation—expanding 206 verified reference sites into 1,420 total points by generating 6 local vicinity points around each core site to capture surrounding terrain variability.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

• Handling Airless Bodies (Missing Axes): Because the Moon lacks an atmosphere, humidity and atmospheric pressure are unavailable. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts calculations from 8 axes to 6 valid axes without artificially penalizing lunar sites.
• Scientific Integrity & User Control: To prevent synthetic vicinity points from misleading strict scientific queries, every augmented point is explicitly labeled in the Methodology tab and can be filtered out in one click using the “Catalog sites only” toggle to compare exclusively against the 206 baseline sites.
• Accessibility & Performance: Designed as a lightweight, zero-backend client-side web application so scientists and students can run complex multi-dimensional queries instantaneously in any browser.
